newsitem.title: UK: UK gives no breakdown of utility tax liability.
newsitem.headline: UK gives no breakdown of utility tax liability.

text.p: The UK Inland Revenue said on Wednesday it would not give estimates of individual companies' exposure to the windfall tax on privatised utilities announced in Chancellor Gordon Brown's budget.
A Revenue spokeswoman said such estimates would breach its usual confidentiality.
Each company liable to the one-off tax must make a return to the Inland Revenue by December 1, the date when the first half of the tax is due, and include an estimate of its liability.

Brown said in his budget speech the tax would raise a net 4.8 billion stg, including the effects of cutting a levy on gas -- 2.1 billion stg from the electricity sector, around 1.65 billion stg from water companies and 1.45 billion stg from others.

The tax will be charged at 23 percent on the difference between the value of the company when privatised and a valuation of the company in a period of up to four years after flotation based on multiplying average annual profits net of tax by a price/earnings ratio of nine, the Revenue said in a statement.
